brief.topic: A Tangent Can Guess Where a Curve Crosses Zero

s01: We want the positive number whose square is two.
Can the curve help us improve a guess?
Draw y equals x squared minus two.
Start at x equals two.
The curve is two units above zero there, and its slope is four.
Follow the tangent line down to the horizontal axis.
Dropping two at a slope of four means moving left by one half.
The next guess is one and a half.
At that point the curve is one quarter above zero, and its slope is three.
The next correction is one twelfth.
Our new guess is seventeen twelfths, about one point four one six seven.
Each step replaces the nearby curve by its tangent and solves the simpler linear problem.
This is Newton's method: subtract the function value divided by its derivative.
For this curve, the update is the average of x and two divided by x.
Starting from two, the guesses approach the square root of two.
But a tangent is a local approximation, not a universal promise.
Start at zero instead.
The tangent is horizontal and never reaches the axis, so the formula divides by zero.
Choosing a starting point matters.
The geometry explains both the quick improvement and this failure.

scenes.narration:
We want the positive number whose square is two. Can the curve help us improve a guess?

Draw y equals x squared minus two. Start at x equals two. The curve is two units above zero there, and its slope is four.

Follow the tangent line down to the horizontal axis. Dropping two at a slope of four means moving left by one half. The next guess is one and a half.

At that point the curve is one quarter above zero, and its slope is three. The next correction is one twelfth. Our new guess is seventeen twelfths, about one point four one six seven.

Each step replaces the nearby curve by its tangent and solves the simpler linear problem. This is Newton's method: subtract the function value divided by its derivative.

For this curve, the update is the average of x and two divided by x. Starting from two, the guesses approach the square root of two.

But a tangent is a local approximation, not a universal promise. Start at zero instead. The tangent is horizontal and never reaches the axis, so the formula divides by zero. Choosing a starting point matters. The geometry explains both the quick improvement and this failure.
